_comment: What an sglang PD-disaggregated manifest from mad-slurm-multinode needs added to become measurable. Merge into the base manifest, do not use standalone: `jq -s '.[0] * .[1]' base.json sglang-disagg.overlay.json > run_manifest_prof.json`. Fill every <FILL_...> first, and add the /run_logs bind by hand as the README describes -- it is an edit to a string the base manifest already has, which a merge cannot express. PROFILE_ENABLE=1 is the single switch: MAD's scripts/sglang_disagg/sglang_disagg_mori_io_ep.sh reads it and adds --disable-custom-all-reduce to both roles and --disable-cuda-graph to decode, in the MODEL_CONFIG strings every node interpolates. Setting those flags at a launch site instead profiled three nodes out of four (job 25824). Explanations live in _comment_* keys beside a block, never inside it: madengine turns each key of an env block into a variable.

context._comment_tools: Kept for symmetry with the training overlay. On this cluster serving runs produced no rocprofv3 CSVs at all even with a graceful shutdown, so their reports are volume-only and expected to be; drop the block unless kernel durations are being chased. <FILL_PROF_ROOT> is a shared-FS directory for this run's profiling artifacts, e.g. /shared/rundir/prof_sgl_llama70b_2p2d.

tools.name: rocprofv3_communication
tools.cmd: bash -c 'set -o pipefail; host=$(hostname); local_dir=/tmp/rocprof_$host; out_dir=<FILL_PROF_ROOT>/rocprof/$host; mkdir -p "$local_dir" "$out_dir"; bash ../scripts/common/tools/rocprof_wrapper.sh --kernel-trace --rccl-trace --stats --output-format csv -d "$local_dir" -- "$@"; rc=$?; find "$local_dir" -name "*_stats.csv" -exec cp {} "$out_dir/" \; ; rm -rf "$local_dir"; exit $rc' _

context._comment_docker_env_vars: The base template ships NCCL_DEBUG=WARN, which logs nothing to parse. SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR is what makes /start_profile write anything: without it the profile point is a silent no-op. RCCL_LOG_DIR gives each server process its own RCCL file (NCCL_DEBUG_FILE) instead of eight ranks overwriting each other in one stdout, which is where the torn records and the invented topology edges come from; it must sit under /run_logs so the analysis outside the container can read it. PROFILE_ROLES decides which reports exist, one per role, and the role's log is also where the tooling reads which trace directory belongs to which role. PROFILE_CONCURRENCY matches the benchmark point being characterised.

deployment_config._comment_env_vars: The same variables at launcher level: a value set only here never reaches the workload, and a value set only in the container block is missing from the sbatch environment.
